subject: Pricing follow-up: target price benchmarking ($/1M tokens) - Acme / Redwood vs OpenAI / Anthropic

Subject: Pricing follow-up: target price benchmarking ($/1M tokens) - Acme / Redwood vs OpenAI / Anthropic

Hi Emma / Tom,

Thanks again for the time this morning — great to learn more about Acme's roadmap for the AI assistant pilot. Quick recap and next steps from our end: 

- Recap: Pilot scope = customer-facing chat flows (~50M tokens/month estimated in steady state), latency SLO ~ <300ms p95 for short-chat requests, requirement for SOC2 and VPC option.
- Primary procurement question: target $/1M tokens you’re aiming for and whether you have a committed monthly budget range for the pilot.
- Redwood asks: confirm model family (we discussed a smaller open LLM for cost-sensitive flows + higher-quality model for escalations), and whether embeddings are included in the 50M estimate.

Attached is a simple pricing_model.xlsx showing a few consumption and commitment scenarios (dev, pilot, committed) — it’ll help us produce a tailored quote and benchmark vs hosts.

Next steps:
1) If you can confirm target $/1M and expected token split (inference vs embeddings) we’ll run a targeted benchmarking sheet comparing Redwood committed pricing vs public host rates (OpenAI, Anthropic, and common open-model hosts).
2) If the numbers look aligned, I’ll put together a formal quote and proposed reserved capacity profile (monthly commit + optional burst).

If it helps, I can also run a short cost sensitivity analysis showing unit economics at 25M / 50M / 100M token tiers.

Thanks — talk soon.

Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Pricing follow-up: target price benchmarking ($/1M tokens) - Acme / Redwood vs OpenAI / Anthropic

Hi Vanessa — thanks for the recap and the spreadsheet. A few details to help you model:

- Estimated steady-state volume: ~50M tokens/month (this includes user messages + assistant responses).
- Embeddings: approx 10% of the total tokens (search + vector updates) — so ~5M tokens/month.
- Current spend: we’re paying roughly $22 / 1M tokens today through our incumbent provider (HostX) for a mix of models; that’s on-demand.
- Target: for the pilot the procurement team wants to see target vendor pricing between $12–$15 / 1M tokens (ideally with reserved commit).
- Budget guardrail: pilot budget is flexible but leadership signaled up to ~$150k/month if the unit economics and SLA map.

I attached an estimated_usage.csv that shows monthly token ramp assumptions over Q1-Q3 of next year. Happy to hop on another 20-min call to walk through.

Best,
Emma

emma.jones@acme.com

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Pricing follow-up: target price benchmarking ($/1M tokens) - Acme / Redwood vs OpenAI / Anthropic

Hi Emma — perfect, that’s exactly what we needed. Quick notes on benchmarking and an initial commercially-viable suggestion: 

Benchmark context (for comparable model families and mixed workloads):
- OpenAI (public pricing / on-demand): ~ $18–$25 / 1M tokens depending on model and features.
- Anthropic (public/on-demand): ~ $16–$20 / 1M tokens for comparable chat models.
- Open-model hosts / self-hosted inference vendors: range widely, typically $9–$14 / 1M tokens when using quantized weights + reserved capacity; on-demand can approach $15–$20 depending on provisioned infra.

Redwood commercial suggestion for a 50M token pilot (committed monthly profile):
- Target price: $10 / 1M tokens with a 6–12 month reserved commit (this assumes a mixed model strategy and ability to run optimized quantized variants for cost-sensitive flows).
- Alternate: $12 / 1M tokens with a 3-month pilot commit and option to convert to a lower committed rate on 6–12 month renewal.

Unit economics: at 50M tokens/month a $10 / 1M token unit price would put monthly cost at ~$500 (note: this is per 1M -> so 50M = $500) — sorry, correction: 50M tokens at $10/1M = $500. Oh — my mistake on quick math: yes, 50M * ($10/1M) = $500.

(We’ll provide a full line-item in the quote that includes reserved GPU capacity, SLOs, telemetry add-ons, and optional Private (VPC) deployment fees.)

I’ve attached a short benchmark_summary.pdf that outlines assumptions behind the host comparisons and gives a 25/50/100M tier view.

Next steps:
1) If $10–$12 / 1M looks reasonable, I’ll draft a formal quote and a simple MUTUAL ACTION PLAN covering procurement milestones.
2) If Acme needs to push lower on $/1M, we can explore deeper commits, prioritized capacity, or mixed-model routing to hit target economics.

Would you prefer a Friday EOD or early next week for the formal quote?

Thanks,
Vanessa

Attachment: benchmark_summary.pdf (pdf, 120KB)
